Correct the earlier unauthorized removal of Google Analytics, restore GA4 to both public sites, and make complete page-URL reporting—including imported URLs in query parameters—the explicit owner-selected policy.

## Evidence collected

- Historical configuration proves WebNR already used GA4 measurement `G-DGH8HNQKE4` before the product-rescue change.
- Pull request #19 removed GA4 based on agent preference rather than an owner instruction. The user explicitly rejected that decision and required analytics on every site.
- The owner further specified that WebNR must send the complete page URL, including query parameters and imported URLs in `?add=...`.
- The application implements full URL reporting through `page_location: window.location.href` and `page_path: window.location.pathname + window.location.search`.

- Google signals and ad-personalization signals remain disabled without reducing full page-URL reporting.
- Book content and reading progress stay in browser storage. No custom analytics events containing local file contents or reading progress were added.
- The shared `AutoArchive/seo-skill` previously lacked a mandatory runtime-analytics contract and therefore did not prevent autonomous removal.
- The new shared validator enforces an `## Analytics` section, a named provider, a public verification URL, required Search Console, an explicit payload policy, and an owner-selected `full-url` or `path-only` mode.
- The first shared-skill CI attempt correctly failed because the new skill lacked `agents/openai.yaml`; the missing metadata was added on the same branch and later validation passed.
- Earlier product work also confirmed and repaired unreachable first-use import, blocking dialogs, accessibility defects, destructive Service Worker behavior, conflicting Next.js configuration, obsolete dependencies, false EPUB support, and weak documentation/deployment evidence.

## Decisions and follow-ups

- Every managed site must have analytics; an agent may not remove it based on preference.
- Analytics behavior is owner controlled and recorded in `site.md`.
- WebNR's required mode is `full-url`; complete browser URLs and query parameters must be sent to GA4.
- WebNR public documentation must clearly disclose that imported URLs in `?add=...` are included in reported page URLs.
- A runtime script tag alone is not proof. Source, generated output, exact production deployment, public loader/configuration, and later provider evidence must all be checked.
- Missing GA4 or Search Console exports are missing evidence, not zero traffic.
- Existing documentation-deployment and permanent production-evidence work remains active and must not be bypassed.
- Future product priorities remain backup/restore, IndexedDB migrations, E2E/accessibility/offline tests, stable releases, real EPUB parsing, and versioned clean-room Legado compatibility fixtures.
